summary: A Slack app that installs into your own workspace works the moment you finish OAuth setup: define scopes, add a redirect URL, and run the install flow. No review is needed to use the app privately. Listing publicly in the Slack Marketplace is optional and adds a substantial review that can run many weeks, including a hard prerequisite of 10+ active workspaces before you may submit.

oauthAvailability.note: Slack uses OAuth 2.0 for installation. Private installs need no review; a Marketplace listing is optional.

difficulty.reason: Scope and installation setup is straightforward, but public Marketplace listing adds a long optional review with strict prerequisites.

approvalWait.note: Zero for private installs. Marketplace listing adds up to ~10 weeks.

timeEstimate.criticalPath: OAuth setup is fast; the optional Marketplace review is the long pole if you choose to list.

review.requiredWhen: Only required to list the app in the Slack Marketplace. Private/distributed installs do not need review.

stages.name: Preliminary review

duration.note: Up to 10 business days for feedback.

stages.description: Slack's Marketplace team gives initial feedback on the submission and listing.

stages.name: Functional review
stages.description: Up to 10 weeks for new submissions (up to 6 weeks for published-app resubmissions). Requires 10+ active workspaces before submitting.

prerequisites.item: A Slack workspace you can install into
prerequisites.detail: You need a workspace to create and test the app.

prerequisites.item: An app created in the Slack developer portal
prerequisites.detail: Create the app, then configure OAuth scopes and a redirect URL.
An active workspace is one used in the past 28 days; apps below this are blocked from submitting.

steps.title: Create a Slack app and add OAuth scopes
steps.detail: Create a new app in the Slack developer portal, then under OAuth & Permissions add the bot and/or user scopes your app needs.

steps.title: Add a redirect URL and build the install flow
steps.detail: Register an HTTPS redirect URL, then send admins to the authorize endpoint. Exchange the returned code at oauth.v2.access for bot and user tokens.
steps.gotcha: Bot and user tokens are returned in different parts of the oauth.v2.access response; store the right one for each API call.

steps.title: Install to your workspace and verify
steps.detail: Run the install flow against a non-development workspace as a new customer would, confirming installation, onboarding, and uninstall all work end to end.

steps.title: Optional: submit for Marketplace review
steps.detail: From the Submit to the Slack Marketplace section of the app's config, review your listing, scopes, and test credentials, pass automated checks, then submit. You must already have 10+ active workspaces.

notes: Redirect URLs must be HTTPS and are registered under OAuth & Permissions.
The redirect_uri in the authorize request must match a registered URL.

recommended.purpose: Post messages as the app's bot user.
List public channels in the workspace.
Look up basic user profile information.

sensitive.consequence: Admin scopes grant workspace/org administration; reviewed closely and only for Enterprise Grid admin apps.
Reads message content in public channels; justify in the Marketplace review.

notes: Request the minimum scopes; reviewers check that each scope maps to a feature.
Leftover test slash commands or unused scopes commonly cause review returns.

blockers.title: Blocked from Marketplace submission
blockers.symptom: You cannot submit the app to the Marketplace.
blockers.cause: The app has fewer than 10 active workspaces (used in the last 28 days).
blockers.resolution: Grow adoption to 10+ active workspaces before submitting; this threshold is enforced at submission.

blockers.title: Submission returned as not ready
blockers.symptom: Slack returns the submission and asks for more work before resubmitting.
blockers.cause: Bugs, poor UX, or the app was submitted while still in beta or partially tested.
blockers.resolution: Ship a production-ready, fully tested build; run the full install/onboarding/uninstall flow as a new customer first.

blockers.title: invalid redirect_uri on install
blockers.symptom: The install flow errors on the redirect step.
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri is not an exact match to a registered HTTPS redirect URL.
blockers.resolution: Register the exact HTTPS redirect URL under OAuth & Permissions and retry.

agentCan: Implement the oauth.v2.access code exchange and token storage
Wire scopes, slash commands, and the redirect route
humanMust: Create and own the Slack app configuration
Grow to 10+ active workspaces before any Marketplace submission
Submit for review and respond to reviewer feedback
handoffPoints: Agent builds and tests the install flow; a human decides on and drives any Marketplace listing.

difficulty.note: Private install is review-free; Marketplace review is optional and documented.

timeEstimate.note: Hands-on is an estimate; review durations are from the review guide.

review.note: Review timelines and prerequisites from the Marketplace review guide.

prerequisites.note: 10+ active workspaces prerequisite documented in the review guide.

steps.note: Install steps follow the installing-with-oauth guide.

redirectUris.note: Redirect URL handling from the OAuth install guide.

scopes.note: Scope names are standard Slack scopes; selection is author guidance.

blockers.note: Submission blockers (workspace threshold, readiness) documented in the review guide.

agentHandoff.note: Author judgment on the agent/human split.
